items.summary: June 11 evening closes at the most geopolitically significant unverified event of the conflict cycle: multiple sources report NATO forces intercepted and destroyed Iranian drones and missiles approaching Incirlik Air Base in southern Turkey, with at least one Iranian ballistic missile engaged by NATO air defense systems after entering Turkish airspace. The events remain officially unconfirmed through NATO, Pentagon, and Turkish MoD channels as of close of the evening cycle — no formal statement, Article 5 consultation signal, or CENTCOM repositioning order has been issued. If confirmed, this constitutes the first direct Iranian military incursion into NATO territory in the Hormuz conflict and the most significant geographic escalation of the war, engaging the collective defense provisions of the NATO treaty and requiring a formal Alliance response. The confirmation or denial is the primary overnight watch item. Concurrent with this escalation report, Trump stated in remarks attributed to a post-Putin call that 'the war is very complete, pretty much' and that the Strait of Hormuz was open — claims categorically inconsistent with the operational status through the evening cycle: Hormuz remains closed (Day 104 of the naval blockade), no CENTCOM stand-down has been issued, the MOU remains unsigned, and no transition to open-passage operations has been confirmed by CENTCOM, State, or IRGC. The statement is assessed as diplomatic signaling, negotiating posture, or a characterization of back-channel talks by an interlocutor — not a confirmed operational status change. If the claim reflects genuine back-channel progress, it would be the first leader-level proximity signal since the May 26 Khamenei endorsement reporting; absent operational confirmation, it does not meet the threshold for a Vibe upgrade. MOU amendment counter-demand advances to Day 7 with no new Iranian formal response — seven consecutive cycle days since the Sunday June 7 signing window's passage without recovery catalyst, acceptance signal, new signing timeline, or formal rejection. Iran comms resolved advances to Day 8 — channel integrity confirmed, no re-suspension signal in the evening cycle. The inaugural June 16-17 meeting is the first real-world test of his policy orientation; the 10-member FOMC dissent calculus and June 17 statement language constitute the primary market signal. items.summary: Four secondary infrastructure threads entering June 11 evening. First: NSF Newport OR ocean observatory (last remaining PNW floating station after Washington stations removed September 2025) continues advancing toward end-of-June removal — approximately three weeks before structural monitoring loss. Loss of this station will degrade atmospheric river early detection, marine heat wave and fisheries forecasting, wave height/storm surge coastal emergency management, and Pacific maritime monitoring capacity at precisely the peak summer maritime stress period. Second: US grid demand is rising at the fastest pace since World War II, driven by AI data center build-out. The electric utility sector faces unprecedented load growth challenging both physical infrastructure and the regulatory and market structures governing grid development for decades. Globally, approximately $5.8 trillion is forecast for grid upgrades between 2026-2035; US alone faces approximately $1 trillion in grid modernization needs over the next decade. DOE's national energy emergency (declared 2025) remains operative — aging plants held online, interconnection queue expediting under emergency authority. Interconnection queues at historic levels with gigawatts of ready-to-build projects waiting years for connection studies. Battery storage deployment accelerating nationally (2026 tracking above 2025's 10+ GW record-breaking pace) but transmission bottlenecks limit integration velocity. Third: FERC summer assessment confirms PNW drought-reduced hydropower as a specific summer grid vulnerability — BPA output reduction concurrent with above-normal temperature and below-normal precipitation forecast through June. Fourth: Sound Transit's $34.5B funding gap remains unresolved heading into the June board capital planning session; Link Light Rail (primary Lumen Field transit mode) is T-4 to the first Seattle match (June 15); no board capital resolution or federal match alternative confirmed.
